miniProject.title: Tree core, one neighbor or kernel mechanism, and a family-choice defense
miniProject.brief: Implement a deterministic CART core with one ensemble and one neighbor or kernel mechanism in NumPy in your own repository, test them against hand cases and scikit-learn, configure the boosting libraries on one fixed split, and defend a family choice from geometry, uncertainty, interpretability, fit cost and prediction cost.
steps: Build the CART core: Gini and entropy impurity, an exhaustive split scan with a stated threshold and tie rule, growth limits (max_depth, min_samples_leaf) and prediction. Match hand cases, then DecisionTreeClassifier predictions on tie-free data with matching limits.
Prune by cost complexity: take the \(\alpha\) path and choose \(\alpha\) by cross-validation on the training split only.
Add bagging or a random forest over your core. Show validation error and its spread over seeds against the number of trees, next to a single tree.

Add one neighbor or kernel mechanism: kNN with a stated tie rule and a scaled-versus-unscaled test, a Pegasos kernel SVM, or an RBF kernel matrix with a positive semidefinite check. Compare predictions with KNeighborsClassifier or SVC on a fixed split.

On one fixed tabular split, configure HistGradientBoosting and XGBoost, LightGBM and CatBoost from their parameter pages with early stopping on a validation split. State each library's categorical handling and record the best iteration, validation score, fit time and predict time.
Add a random high-cardinality column and compare impurity (MDI) importance with permutation importance on held-out data.

Defend a family choice: compare a tree, an ensemble, a boosting model, kNN and an SVM on the same split with paired uncertainty on the validation metric, plus calibration, interpretability, fit cost and prediction cost. Name the condition that would reverse the choice.
deliverables: The tree package: impurity, split search, growth limits, pruning and the ensemble, with tests.
The neighbor or kernel mechanism with its differential tests.
The family-choice dossier: one comparison table with paired uncertainty and costs, the boosting-library runs, the importance comparison, the decision and its tripwire.

checks.name: Deep-ML 138, 20, 307, 21 and 280
checks.note: Public tests. Pass the ones matching your mechanisms after your local tests do; the cards state each convention the tests pin, such as raw-value thresholds in 138 and in-place per-sample updates in 21.

rubric.pass: Impurity and split search match hand cases, and predictions match scikit-learn on tie-free data.
rubric.strong: Property tests cover ties under a documented rule, and depth and leaf limits reproduce scikit-learn's node counts.

rubric.pass: The ensemble lowers validation error or its spread over seeds compared with one tree.
rubric.strong: An out-of-bag estimate tracks a held-out estimate, and the report explains any gap.

rubric.pass: Predictions match scikit-learn on a fixed split.
rubric.strong: Tests cover feature scaling and a tie or degenerate-kernel case.

rubric.pass: HistGradientBoosting and at least one of XGBoost, LightGBM or CatBoost run with early stopping and stated categorical handling.
rubric.strong: All three external libraries run, and the report explains the learning-rate and iteration tradeoff from the recorded best iterations.

rubric.pass: One table reports the metric with paired uncertainty, fit time and predict time for each family.
rubric.strong: The choice survives a small change in the best score, and the report names the condition that would reverse it.

miniProject.feedsInto: Milestone artifact 2, the mechanisms suite: the deterministic tree core, the ensemble and the kNN or kernel model come from here. The family-choice comparison feeds the decision dossier.
